newsitem.title: CHINA: JOHNSON FORESEES DOUBLE SALES IN 5 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: JOHNSON FORESEES DOUBLE SALES IN 5 YEARS.

text.p: Micromotor maker Johnson Electric Holdings Ltd, which was dropped from the blue chip Hang Seng Index last month, expects to double its capacity and sales in five years, chairman Patrick Wang said on Tuesday.
"We actually have a feeling that each of the individual five units should be able to double," Wang told reporters after the company's annual general meeting.
"Our feeling is that all the five businesses could be able to expand quite a lot," he said referring to sales and capacity.
Total sales in Johnson rose 18.2 percent to HK$2.60 billion and net profit surged 58.9 percent to HK$437 million for the year ended March 31, 1997.
Johnson principally supplies micromotors to manufacturers under five main categories -- automobile components, home appliances, power tools, personal care and business equipment and multi-media.
Orders-on-hand so far this year were in line the company's internal forecasts, Wang said. "We hope to have a double digit growth this year against last year," he said.
Wang declined to make a profit forecast but said the company was confident of a healthy growth rate.

The depreciation of the Thai Baht should benefit the company since it helped reduce production costs at its Thai factory, he said. "On the profit side, the impact is immaterial as all the products from Thailand are for export," he said.
The company has two major production facilities in southern China and Thailand which have a total production capacity of over one million units per day.
"We are now in peak season and utilisation is close to full capacity," Paul Tong Johnson's financial officer said.
He expected the average utilisation of production facilities would be 90-95 percent this fiscal year.
Wang also said the company planned to invest about HK$200 million to expand its two factories in Thailand and China.
"Multimedia/business equipment should score the highest percentage growth (in sales) this year," Tong said.

Profit margins on the multimedia/business equipment unit grew after the company discontinued a service of attaching certain electronic components to Johnson's micromotors as requested by Customers, Wang said.
One of the reasons that business equipment/multimedia unit would post the highest sales growth was because of its relatively low base, Tong added.
It accounted for only seven percent of the company's total dollar sales in 1996/97, Johnson's annual report said.

Dollar sales to automobile components makers represented about 32 percent of the total in fiscal 1997, home appliances producers 26 percent, power tools maker and personal care applications 23 and 12 percent respectively.

By geographical destination, Johnson saw the fastest growth in the U.S. and Asia. "Sales in the U.S. are expected to grow faster than Europe this year and individual areas in Asia are also growing fast," the chairman said.
Hong Kong and China were its largest market area accounting for about 32 percent of the total turnover in fiscal 1997.
They were followed by Europe and North America, which represented about 29 and 27 percent.
Wang said the company had successfully reduced its Japanese purchases and boosted sales in Japan to help offset fluctuation of the yen.
"We have done a lot and now we are in a position that yen volatility is not an issue for us," he said.
Johnson has been excluded from the blue chip Hang Seng Index since July 31 but Tong said this did not affect their financing cost or share performance.
